- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or shows recent sharp drops, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates short-term rallies after recent lows — add a small upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.5%) to forecast if recent price is falling and sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- Model tends to overestimate long-term trends (30d) after sharp spikes — apply a downward correction of 1–3% if forecasted price is above 10% above recent 18-day high.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings (e.g., -0.25, 0.00, 0.00), model often fails to mean-revert — apply a gentle upward bias to counteract persistent downward drift.  
- Model often lags sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast to rise 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Avoid forecasting below 60% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly bearish — use sentiment as a floor trigger for minimum price.
